CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFERROR

CFERROR sets up a custom error page for the rest of the request. When an error is not caught by CFTRY/CFCATCH, the visitor sees your template instead of KoldFusion's diagnostic message, and the template can use the Error variables to say what went wrong. It is normally placed in Application.cfm so it covers every page of an application.

Category

Exception handling

Syntax

<CFERROR TYPE="Request/Exception/Validation/Monitor"
    TEMPLATE="template_path"
    MAILTO="email_address"
    EXCEPTION="exception_type">

Attributes

TYPE
Optional, default "Request". Which handler to set. Request and Exception are used for uncaught errors; see the usage notes. Validation (form field validation errors) and Monitor are accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores them.
TEMPLATE
Required. The error page, as a path relative to the current template.
MAILTO
Optional. An e-mail address, made available to the error page as Error.MailTo so it can say whom to tell.
EXCEPTION
Optional. Exception type the handler applies to. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion's Exception handler handles every type.

Usage

A Request handler is a plain HTML page: KoldFusion replaces the #Error.xxx# references in it with their values and sends it as is, without processing any other CFML. That makes it safe to use even when things are badly broken. An Exception handler (new in 4.5) is a real CFML page that can query databases, send mail with CFMAIL and so on. When both are set, the Exception handler wins. If the handler itself fails, the standard error message is shown.

The error page has these variables:

Variable Contents
Error.Message, Error.Detail, Error.Type What went wrong
Error.Diagnostics The full diagnostic text of the standard error message
Error.DateTime When the error happened
Error.Template, Error.QueryString The page that failed and its URL parameters
Error.RemoteAddress, Error.Browser, Error.HTTPReferer Who was visiting, with what, from where
Error.MailTo The MAILTO address

Anything the failed page had already generated is discarded. CFERROR only lasts for the current request; a site-wide error template can also be set in the Administrator.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- sn_errorpage.cfm is an Exception handler: a full CFML page --->
<CFERROR TYPE="Exception" TEMPLATE="sn_errorpage.cfm" MAILTO="webmaster@localhost">
<CFPARAM NAME="URL.Crash" DEFAULT="No">

<CFIF URL.Crash>
  <!--- This page is about to fail; the error page takes over --->
  <CFSET Modems = 0>
  <CFSET BaudPerModem = 56000 / Modems>
</CFIF>

<P>All is well. This page has registered <B>sn_errorpage.cfm</B> as its error handler.</P>
<P><A HREF="cferror.cfm?Crash=Yes">Make the page divide by zero</A> and see the custom error
page instead of the standard error message.</P>
